assumptions: Official BZP and TED access remains lawful and sufficiently complete for the chosen vertical.
The product provides decision support with cited source material and preserves human responsibility for final legal and commercial judgment.
Customers consent to using their decisions and outcomes for aggregate calibration.
The initial product remains a standardized vertical subscription rather than expanding into bespoke bid preparation.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots should establish notice frequency, baseline screening and bid hours, extraction precision, false-negative tolerance, decision adoption, measurable hours or losses avoided, subscription renewal, acquisition cost, and the rate at which proprietary outcome labels improve recommendations.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Focusing on the go/no-go decision before bid resources are committed is sharper than another notice alert or generic document summary. A vertical rule set, cited requirement extraction, decision log, and outcome feedback form a coherent product loop around a recurring measurable choice.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Published notices create recurring decision events, and wasted bid preparation or missed deadlines can be expensive for a small team. The actual labor loss, false-negative tolerance, and willingness to pay 499-1,499 PLN monthly rather than use portals or consultants remain unverified.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Advance subscriptions, reusable ingestion, and vertical templates could support high gross margin and low initial capital. The projected customer count and 75-90% contribution margin are not evidence-backed, while onboarding, source QA, support, and the cost of trustworthy extraction may be significant early on.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish SMEs that repeatedly bid in a technical category are a sensible segment with observable workflow frequency. The proposal has not yet named or evidenced the first vertical, its addressable bidder count, bid cost, notice cadence, or propensity to buy.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Vertical calibration and a customer-specific decision record can outperform generic search, but public portals, commercial data reusers, procurement consultants, and AI-enabled software can add similar scoring. No vertical lead or exclusive input currently supports domination.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Once one vertical works, the same decision architecture can extend to adjacent categories, more procurement sources, additional countries, private tenders, and later bid-workflow modules. Expansion must preserve domain precision and should not become bespoke bid writing.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Consented bid/no-bid decisions, eligibility findings, participation, and award outcomes could create a differentiated vertical dataset and switching cost. Owned code alone is weak protection, official inputs are nonexclusive, and early rules can be copied before the outcome loop reaches scale.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The founder can own the scoring software, has relevant language-processing and analytics skills, and can prototype from official access paths without large capital. Competitors have the same raw notices, and no proprietary outcome corpus, customer base, or privileged distribution exists yet.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Official digital feeds and improving document models make a cited, automated screening product feasible now. The same technology also lets incumbent portals and consultants commoditize summarization rapidly, so timing helps execution more than it creates scarcity.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Narrow-sector outbound and referrals from consultants, accountants, associations, and trade groups are plausible low-capital paths to repeat bidders. No channel or paid design partner is committed, and customer acquisition cost is only a target.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A one-vertical prototype is technically and financially feasible within the stated constraints, and human final judgment limits some liability. Reliable parsing across formats, changing source access, legal-advice boundaries, and especially costly false negatives require strong evaluation and cautious product design.

highest_value_structural_change: Select one high-bid-cost technical vertical and make the product an auditable decision system that captures eligibility rules, human overrides, hours avoided, participation, and outcomes for paid design partners, rather than competing as a generic tender-alert interface.
main_structural_strength: A recurring observable notice triggers a costly go/no-go decision, and the venture can own the vertical scoring and outcome-learning workflow while relying on openly accessible rather than privileged source data.
primary_score_limiter: The proposal has not proven that a specific vertical experiences enough avoidable bid cost, trusts automated screening, and will pay and retain at the proposed subscription price despite existing portals and consultants.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: TED explicitly anticipates commercial reuse of its nonexclusive data, while public portals and procurement consultants already own adjacent discovery workflows and can add AI summaries or scoring without depending on this venture.
